1.title: Troubleshooting Tools
1.text: Welcome to Module twenty-four: Troubleshooting Tools. It covers the exam area five point zero Network Troubleshooting. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. five point five Given a scenario, use the appropriate tool or protocol to solve networking issues: software tools (protocol analyzer. Command line: ping, traceroute or tracert, nslookup, tcpdump, dig, netstat, ip or ifconfig or ipconfig, arp. Nmap. L L D P or C D P. Speed tester). Hardware tools (toner, cable tester, taps, Wi-Fi analyzer, visual fault locator). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: five point zero Network Troubleshooting (twenty-four percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: Command-line tools
1.text: Command-line tools. The figure shows this: Which tool answers which question.

1.title: Command-line tools, continued
1.text: Command-line tools. ping. Tests reachability and round-trip time with I C M P echo. traceroute (Linux, mac O S) or tracert (Windows). Shows each hop on the path and where it stops or slows. nslookup. Queries D N S for a name (interactive or one-shot). dig. Detailed D N S queries (Linux, mac O S): record types, which server answered. tcpdump. Command-line packet capture (Linux). netstat. Shows connections, listening ports and statistics on the host. ip (Linux) or ifconfig (older Linux, mac O S) or ipconfig (Windows). Shows or sets I P configuration: address, mask, gateway, ipconfig slash all, slash release, slash renew, slash flushdns. arp. Shows or edits the A R P table (I P to M A C mappings). Exam tip: tracert equals Windows, traceroute equals Linux. ipconfig slash release then slash renew refreshes a D H C P lease. nslookup and dig test D N S only.

1.title: Other software tools
1.text: Other software tools. Protocol analyzer (for example Wireshark). Captures and decodes packets for deep analysis. Nmap. Discovers hosts and scans open ports and services. L L D P or C D P. Neighbor discovery: L L D P is the open standard, C D P is Cisco's; shows which device and port is connected. Speed tester. Measures throughput and latency to a test server.

1.title: Hardware tools
1.text: Hardware tools. Toner (tone generator and probe). Traces a cable through walls and panels to find its other end. Cable tester. Checks continuity, wire map, shorts, opens, miswires. Tap. Copies traffic passively from a link (network tap) for monitoring. Wi-Fi analyzer. Shows signal strength, channels and interference. Visual fault locator (V F L). A red laser that shows breaks and bad connectors in fiber.

1.title: Device commands (generic show commands)
1.text: Device commands (generic show commands). show mac-address-table. Which M A C addresses are learned on which switch ports. show route. The routing table. show interface. Status, speed, duplex, counters (C R C, runts, giants). show config. The running or startup configuration. show arp. The A R P table. show vlan. V L A Ns and port assignments. show power. Po E power budget and consumption. Exam tip: "Which switch port is this M A C on?" equals show mac-address-table. "Is the Po E budget used up?" equals show power. "Interface errors" equals show interface. Exam tip: tracert is Windows, traceroute is Linux; nslookup and dig test D N S; show interface shows error counters.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A technician needs to see each router hop between a P C and a server on Windows. Which command should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: tracert. Tracert is the Windows hop-by-hop tool.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A user can ping an I P address but not the hostname. Which tool helps test D N S? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: nslookup. nslookup queries D N S directly.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An administrator needs to find which switch port a device's M A C address is on. Which command fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: show mac-address-table. The M A C address table maps M A Cs to ports.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A cable run is hidden in the wall and the other end must be found. Which tool helps? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A toner and probe. Toner and probe trace copper cables.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An engineer wants to discover open ports and services on a server. Which tool fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Nmap. Nmap scans hosts for open ports and services.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A technician wants to see which neighboring switch and port is connected to an interface. Which protocol helps? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: L L D P. L L D P and C D P discover directly connected neighbors.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which command renews a D H C P lease on Windows? Answer: ipconfig slash renew (after slash release ). Question two. What does netstat show? Answer: Connections, listening ports and statistics. Question three. What does a visual fault locator find? Answer: Breaks and bad connections in fiber.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which command shows interface counters such as C R C errors? Answer: show interface. Question five. What is the open standard for neighbor discovery? Answer: L L D P. Question six. What does tcpdump do? Answer: Captures packets from the command line.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Reachability: ping, traceroute or tracert. D N S: nslookup, dig. Host info: ipconfig, ifconfig, ip, netstat, arp. Capture and scan: protocol analyzer, tcpdump, Nmap. Hardware: toner, cable tester, tap, Wi-Fi analyzer, visual fault locator. Device commands: show mac-address-table, route, interface, config, arp, vlan, power. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. In the next module, we continue the course.
